title: Runtime 1.21 launch brief — Tiered workload-aware batching defaults (fast / standard / cost-efficient)
body:
Owner: Connor O’Brien (Release Engineering)
DRIs by area (for paging / approvals)
- Runtime + scheduler: Sofia Ivanova
- Feature flag + rollout primitives: Benji Okafor / Jada Williams
- SLOs + on-call / rollback execution: Rafael Mendes
- Dashboards/alerts: Allison Grant / Aisha Bello
- Perf canary + CI stability: Rina Kobayashi / Sahana Iyer
- Evals + quality gate: Jonas Weber
- Product/positioning + external comms: Aditya Rao / Soojin Lee

Release target
- Runtime version: 1.21
- Theme: Workload-aware batching defaults exposed as tier selection (fast / standard / cost-efficient) with safe-by-default guardrails, telemetry, and staged rollout tooling.

What is shipping (scope reminder)
This release adds a batching tier abstraction on top of existing explicit batching knobs, plus:
1) Runtime mapping from tier → scheduler/batching parameters (max_batch, max_queue_delay_ms, prefill/decode weighting, KV cache pressure limits) behind a feature flag.
2) Workload signals made explicit (prompt length buckets, concurrency, streaming vs non-streaming) to avoid “magic” behavior.
3) New metrics for queue delay + batch formation, wired to tracing spans for tail-latency debug.
4) Canary rollout tooling: percentage-based enablement by model + region, with automatic rollback hooks.
5) Config explainability: endpoint/metadata to show effective batching config (tier defaults + any overrides).

Non-goals (explicitly not promised in 1.21)
- Fully automated per-customer bespoke optimization beyond the three tiers.
- New scheduling algorithm research; this is productizing/hardening defaults + guardrails.

Customer impact summary
- Backwards compatibility: Existing explicit batching configs continue to take precedence over tier defaults.
- New behavior only applies when batching_tier is set OR when the flag is enabled for a model/region cohort (see rollout plan).
- Expected outcomes (for standard and cost-efficient cohorts): lower $/1M tokens on non-streaming and high-concurrency workloads, with tier-specific latency targets maintained.
- Risk area: streaming cadence (token delivery jitter) and tail latency during overload; mitigated via tier-specific queue delay caps + overload protection alignment.

Release artifacts included
- Runtime 1.21 release notes entry (internal + external snippet coordinated with Product)
- Updated dashboards/alerts pack for tier monitoring
- Runbook additions: tiered batching troubleshooting + rollback

------------------------------------------------------------
Launch decision framework (go/no-go)

Launch criteria (must be true to proceed to ramp beyond internal canary)
A) CI/perf canary health
- perf-canary/pr_622 jobs green for top model families on at least 2 GPU SKUs (baseline vs tiered profiles)
- No p95 regression beyond thresholds for the intended tier (see SLO guardrails below)
- No new flakiness introduced (Sahana to sign off for release train)

B) Evals / quality gate
- Prompt-set coverage run completed for v1 corpus on the set of launch models
- Quality deltas within guardrails (Jonas to sign off). Note: batching can change timing; the gate uses repeated sampling where necessary.

C) Observability ready
- Dashboards deployed (observability-pack/pr_289) and validated in staging
- Alert routing configured with correct ownership per tier (Rafael/Allison sign-off)
- Effective-config explain output available so support can validate what is actually active

D) Rollback readiness
- Flag controls validated (enable/disable by model/region, % ramp)
- Auto-rollback triggers wired and tested in staging
- Human-in-the-loop rollback path documented and exercised (tabletop)

If any of A–D not met by branch cut, 1.21 can still ship, but tiered batching remains “off by default” (flag hard-disabled) until readiness is complete.

------------------------------------------------------------
SLO tier targets (operational contract)
(Reference: Confluence SLO tier doc; values here reflect current working targets for launch monitoring.)

Fast tier
- Intended use: latency-critical interactive chat + streaming
- Primary objective: minimize queue delay, prioritize decode cadence stability
- Guardrail intent: avoid queue buildup; lower batch sizes
- Monitoring focus: token cadence jitter, p95/p99 end-to-end latency, cancellation rates

Standard tier
- Intended use: default for most hosted workloads; balanced cost and latency
- Monitoring focus: p95 latency and throughput improvements vs baseline, stable error rates

Cost-efficient tier
- Intended use: background/non-interactive workloads, offline processing, high concurrency non-streaming
- Monitoring focus: $/token reduction, GPU utilization, overload protection interactions
- Additional guardrails: load shedding / admission control must prevent timeout spikes

For this launch brief we rely on “no worse than baseline” on error rates and timeouts, and tier-specific latency regression thresholds enforced by canary + on-call policy. Exact numeric thresholds are tracked in the SRE SLO doc and alert definitions.

------------------------------------------------------------
Risk assessment

Top risks (ranked) + mitigations

1) Tail latency regression due to queue delay defaults (esp. when concurrency spikes)
- Failure mode: increased p95/p99 due to queueing under mixed workloads; customers see timeouts.
- Mitigation:
  - Tier-specific max_queue_delay_ms caps
  - Admission control integration + load shedding reason codes (cost-efficient tier alignment)
  - Auto-rollback on sustained p95/p99 regression signals
  - Ramp plan starts with non-streaming routes and known workload distributions
- Owner: Rafael (rollback policy), Sofia (parameters)

2) Streaming cadence regression in fast tier (token delivery jitter)
- Failure mode: first-token latency or token cadence jitter increases; perceived “stutter.”
- Mitigation:
  - Fast tier decode prioritization adjustments + regression test (covered by scheduler fixes)
  - Streaming-specific guardrails: stricter queue delay and decode scheduling weights
  - Canary includes streaming cadence checks
- Owner: Sofia / Leila

3) Model-family/GPU SKU differences cause “one-size default” to be wrong
- Failure mode: OOM risk (KV cache pressure), degraded throughput, unpredictable behavior on certain SKUs.
- Mitigation:
  - Model registry stores tier defaults by model family (and GPU SKU where needed)
  - Conservative defaults at launch; tune post-beta
  - Explicit overrides remain available for internal services and enterprise customers
- Owner: Omar / Ethan

4) Debuggability gaps (support + SE can’t tell what is active)
- Failure mode: support escalations due to confusion tier vs explicit knobs; slow MTTR.
- Mitigation:
  - Effective config explain endpoint/metadata shipped
  - Add support-facing troubleshooting checklist and “common failure modes” notes
- Owner: Connor (release), Miguel (feedback)

5) Alert noise from new queue delay metrics
- Failure mode: page fatigue; false positives during normal traffic patterns.
- Mitigation:
  - Start alerts as “ticket/notify” during early ramps; page only on correlated signals (timeouts + sustained p95)
  - Use burn-rate style alerting for SLO violation rather than raw metric spikes
- Owner: Allison / Aisha

------------------------------------------------------------
Rollout plan (flag + ramp)

Feature flag and control surface
- Flag name (internal): tiered_batching_defaults (runtime)
- Control dimensions:
  - model (family/variant)
  - region
  - route type (chat/completions/embeddings) where supported
  - cohort percentage

Phased ramp (recommended)
Phase 0 — Internal only (dogfood)
- 0–1% traffic, internal services + Redwood test tenants
- Regions: 1 low-risk region first (e.g., us-east)
- Models: 1–2 popular models with stable perf history
- Duration: minimum 24h including peak

Phase 1 — Limited beta (external opt-in)
- Customers opt in via Console/API config (batching_tier) while the default flag remains off globally
- Support readiness: templated response + runbook link + effective-config instructions

Phase 2 — Staged default enablement (standard tier)
- Enable standard tier as default for a small model/region slice (e.g., 5% → 25% → 50% → 100%)
- Keep fast tier explicit opt-in at first for streaming-heavy customers
- Keep cost-efficient tier explicit opt-in until overload protection + alerting confidence is high

Phase 3 — Expand coverage
- Add additional models, SKUs, and regions; consider enabling cost-efficient for select non-streaming routes by default where appropriate

Stop conditions during ramp (immediate hold)
- Sustained increase in timeout rate or cancellation/timeout ratio above baseline
- p95/p99 regression beyond tier guardrails for 2 consecutive windows
- Increase in OOM or GPU memory pressure events correlated with tier enablement
- Spike in support escalations citing latency/timeout regressions

------------------------------------------------------------
Monitoring checklist (what to watch during ramp)

Primary dashboards (per tier, per model, per region)
- End-to-end latency: p50/p95/p99
- Queue delay: histogram + p95 queue wait
- Batch formation:
  - batch size distribution (prefill and decode where tracked)
  - batch fill time / batch wait
- Throughput: tokens/sec, requests/sec
- GPU utilization and memory pressure (KV cache)
- Error rates:
  - 5xx
  - timeouts
  - cancellations
  - load shed events with reason codes
- Streaming cadence (fast tier):
  - time-to-first-token
  - token inter-arrival / jitter proxy metrics

Who watches what
- On-call during ramp window: SRE (Rafael) + runtime shadow (Sofia delegate)
- Release coordination: Connor

Reporting cadence
- At each ramp step (e.g., 5%→25%): post a short update in #eng-releases with:
  - current cohort size
  - deltas vs baseline for p95, timeout rate, GPU util
  - any notable anomalies + decision (continue/hold/rollback)

------------------------------------------------------------
Rollback plan (fast + safe)

Rollback principles
- Prefer “flag off” rollback (no code rollback) unless there is evidence the runtime binary itself is unstable.
- Rollback must be reversible and auditable (who toggled, when, what scope).

Rollback levels (in order)
Level 1: Reduce cohort percentage
- Action: drop from current % to prior stable % (e.g., 50%→25%→5%)
- Use when: mild regression, unclear causality, want to stabilize while investigating
- Owner: SRE on-call (Rafael) with release eng awareness

Level 2: Disable by model/region
- Action: set cohort to 0% for impacted model(s)/region(s)
- Use when: regression clearly correlated with a specific model or region
- Owner: SRE on-call

Level 3: Global disable
- Action: set flag to 0% globally; revert any “default standard tier” enablement
- Use when: widespread regressions or unknown blast radius
- Owner: SRE on-call, notify Connor + Mateo

Level 4: Runtime rollback (binary)
- Action: revert runtime to 1.20.x (or previous patch) per standard runtime rollback procedure
- Use when: issues persist with flag off or additional critical regressions present
- Owner: Release Engineering (Connor) + Infra deployment owner

Auto-rollback hooks
- Trigger candidates (initial): sustained p95 regression + correlated timeout increase, or load shed spike + customer-visible errors
- Note: During Phase 0/1, keep auto-rollback enabled but with conservative sensitivity; prefer human confirmation before global disable.

Post-rollback steps
- Freeze further ramps
- Capture incident summary: scope, metrics, suspected cause, links to traces, mitigation taken
- Open follow-up ticket(s): parameter tuning or bugfix PR, plus an eval/perf canary addition to prevent recurrence

------------------------------------------------------------
Comms plan

Internal comms
1) Branch cut announcement (T-2 days)
- Channel: #eng-releases
- Content:
  - runtime-1.21 branch cut time
  - list of tiered batching PRs included
  - reminder: feature remains behind flag; no default change without explicit ramp approval

2) Ramp announcements (during beta/default enablement)
- Channel: #eng-releases + #eng-runtime + #eng-sre
- Include: cohort %, models/regions, monitoring links, stop conditions, on-call owners

3) Exec/stakeholder update
- Recipients: Mateo Alvarez, Priya Natarajan, Aditya Rao
- Frequency: at Phase 1 start and any rollback event

External comms (customer-facing)
- For beta:
  - Release notes: “Workload-aware batching tiers (beta) — opt-in”
  - Docs: explain tiers + how to choose + how overrides work + expected tradeoffs
  - Support enablement: macro with steps to confirm effective config + what metrics to share

- For default enablement (standard tier):
  - Small note in release notes / changelog for affected cohorts
  - Console tooltip + link to docs; “standard tier is now the default for select models/regions”

Support + SE enablement
- Provide a 1-pager snippet:
  - How to confirm tier (effective-config)
  - What to do if customer reports timeouts (switch to standard/fast or set explicit max_queue_delay)
  - How to capture data for escalation (request IDs, model, region, route, concurrency profile)

------------------------------------------------------------
Schedule (release train placeholders; update in #eng-releases)
- T-7 to T-3: final perf canary + eval runs; dashboards validation in staging
- T-2: branch cut for runtime-1.21; confirm included PR set
- T-1: staging validation; tabletop rollback drill
- T0: runtime-1.21 deploy (flag off by default unless explicitly approved)
- T+1 to T+7: Phase 0 internal canary; then Phase 1 external beta (opt-in)

------------------------------------------------------------
Approval checklist (sign-offs)
- Runtime readiness (scheduler/metrics/tests): Sofia Ivanova
- SRE readiness (alerts + rollback policy): Rafael Mendes
- Observability dashboards verified: Allison Grant
- Perf canary green + stable: Rina Kobayashi / Sahana Iyer
- Evals gate complete: Jonas Weber
- Product comms + docs ready for beta: Aditya Rao / Elliot Price

Notes / open items at time of last edit
- Confirm initial model/region list for Phase 0 canary with SRE + runtime (avoid historically noisy regions)
- Ensure effective-config output is surfaced in Console (at least linkable) before broad beta
- Decide whether cost-efficient tier remains “explicit opt-in only” through entire 1.21 cycle (recommended) pending more overload protection confidence
